free_tier.stated: no service and no account; the reference userspace implementation

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: none

tooling: go build; wg and wg-quick for configuration
chaining: the substrate for the WebSocket forks; on its own it composes only with a peer that accepts UDP.
binding_note: it creates a TUN interface and speaks UDP; a UDP block stops it, so it adds no egress path
reliability_note: upstream mirror lags git.zx2c4.com; the Linux kernel module is the faster path where it exists
confidence_note: the verdict concerns egress only; this is the implementation every WebSocket fork starts from

evidence.proved: "This is an implementation of WireGuard in Go" and the wireguard-go wg0 / wg(8) usage
"Mirror only. Official repository is at https://git.zx2c4.com/wireguard-go"; 4465 stars; last push 2026-10-06; no GitHub releases
on Linux the README says to use the kernel module instead, "which is faster and better integrated into the OS"

notes: As shipped it is UDP only, so it is not a wrapper. It is also the tool that makes a standard .conf usable on a platform with no kernel WireGuard, which is the case for Windows and for containers on hosts without the module.

extras.wg_detail: "With wireguard-go, instead simply run: wireguard-go wg0 ... When an interface is running, you may use wg(8) to configure it", so the standard configuration applies unchanged
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: carries the tunnel over UDP to the configured endpoint
extras.hosting_requirement: none beyond the device; needs a reachable UDP peer
extras.last_release: no GitHub release objects; last push 2026-10-06
